Public transport access is especially strong, with a mobility percentile of 90.64. The regional standard specifies 6 sqm per child of net useful area across designated activity, rest, and toilet spaces; this is not a gross-area threshold, and the supplied data do not confirm the required room layout or net area. Compatibility with the host facility and all planning, building, health, accessibility, fire-safety where required, structural, and authorization checks remain to be verified. Check which regulatory requirements apply when the application is submitted, given the stated transition to newer rules.
pros: Existing school and educational use is closely aligned with the proposed spring section and host-kindergarten context.
The 3,021 sqm gross area substantially exceeds the user's 180 sqm search criterion, though net usable space and room layout still require verification.
Public transport proximity is a strong match, with a mobility percentile of 90.64.
cons: The data do not establish that the building contains the required net useful area in the specified activity, rest, and toilet spaces or that the layout can support the section.
Compatibility with Turin planning rules, building-use authorization, health and accessibility requirements, applicable safety provisions, and sector authorization remains unverified.
Energy performance is a relative weakness: class D, energy score total 8, envelope score 1, and no recorded renewable sources.

evaluation_results.evaluation_text: This 2020 educational property in Turin is a strong strategic candidate for integrating a spring section into an existing kindergarten. Its recorded gross floor area of 7,080.07 sqm is well above the requested 180 sqm, and the verified capacity range of 6–20 children includes the target of 14. The mobility percentile of 90.93 supports the preference for good public transport access. However, the supplied data do not establish the available net usable area, room layout, authorization, or technical suitability for the proposed section. The 6 sqm per child regional standard applies to the combined net usable areas for specified functions, not to the whole property; the applicable requirements at the application date and all listed regulatory checks need confirmation.
pros: Existing educational use and 2020 construction align well with the intended integration into a kindergarten.
Recorded gross floor area of 7,080.07 sqm exceeds the requested 180 sqm, while the verified capacity range of 6–20 children includes 14.
Mobility percentile of 90.93 is consistent with the preference for strong public transport proximity.
cons: The property data do not show whether sufficient net usable area and suitable room arrangements are available for the spring section’s functions.
Urban planning compatibility, building-use authorization, hygiene, accessibility, fire safety where required, structural safety, and sector authorization all require verification.
The energy profile is mixed: class A1 is a strength, while the recorded plant and renewable energy subscores are 1 each and the envelope subscore is 3.

evaluation_results.evaluation_text: This 535.56 sqm school property, built in 2020, is a strong candidate for the proposed spring section integrated with a kindergarten. Its educational use and 14-child capacity align with the stated objective and the verified regional capacity range of 6–20 children. The applicable standard specifies 6 sqm per child across designated net-use areas; it is not a minimum gross property area, so the supplied gross floor area alone cannot establish that these spaces are sufficient. Public transport access is a particular strength. Before proceeding, verify integration with a host kindergarten that meets the relevant requirements, planning and building-use compatibility, and all required health, accessibility, fire-safety, structural, and authorization checks. Confirm which regulatory provisions apply when the application is submitted, given the stated transition to the 2025 requirements.
pros: Existing school and educational use, recent 2020 construction, and substantial 535.56 sqm gross area support further assessment for an educational reuse.
The objective’s 14-child capacity falls within the verified regional range of 6–20 children for a spring section.
Mobility proximity is strong (90.93), alongside high recorded access to education (92.3), green areas (93.38), and healthcare (91.42).
cons: The 6 sqm-per-child standard applies to specified net-use areas, not total gross area; room layout and the required usable areas are not provided and need verification.
The spring section must be integrated with a qualifying kindergarten, nursery, or micro-nursery; the data do not establish that a compliant host is available.
Planning compatibility, permitted use, hygiene, accessibility, fire and structural safety, sector authorization, and the applicable regulatory transition require verification.
